doc.title: John Fedchock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 28, 2015

title: Hearing his own playing, and the Eastman bus story
summary: Rowe plays him a recording of himself; he recalls hearing his own solo on the Woody band bus.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Yeah. I’d like to be a plus one. Okay. Here’s one last selection.
Yes. And do you like it.

You know it’s interesting because I remember when I was on Woody’s band, there were some other guys from Eastman that came out after I had joined the band. And they had some recordings of Eastman’s band. And I was sitting, you know we’re all riding in the bus and as most people did at that time you had headphones on and you’d be listening to music. And I remember I was listening and then I heard like somebody playing something else without headphones and it was like a trombone solo and it sounded interesting. I took my headphones off and went, “wow, that’s me.” So I guess I liked it. Sometimes I like hearing myself, sometimes I really don’t. It’s just like listening to your own voice on the answering machine. It never sounds quite like you expect it to sound.
I want to come back to that thought regarding your band too. But —
